chunks: And as for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Nadr-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb from al-Jazzi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

In the case of a man who died and left behind a female slave of his, and he had freed one-third of her, and the executor married her before distributing any of the inheritance: 'That she is valued, and she and her husband are redeemed for the remainder of her price after she is valued; so whatever of manumission or slavery befalls the woman applies to her child.'

Therefore, this report does not contradict the first two reports, because it is understood that if the man did not own anything other than her, he did not have the right to dispose of more than one-third of her. Thus, it follows the same rule as if there were three partners, in that whenever he frees what he owns, the remainder does not become free, according to what we have previously stated. And that which indicates this is what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a freed female slave whose executor marries her before inheritance distribution?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration to resolve apparent contradictions regarding the emancipation of a slave woman by integrating it with the principle that a testator can only dispose of one-third of his estate; thus, if the man owned no other assets, freeing one-third of the slave is treated as freeing the whole for inheritance purposes. The text clarifies that the remaining two-thirds must be redeemed from the estate, and the status of the child follows the mother's ultimate condition after this redemption process.
